meta.note: Single source of truth. `npm run tokens` generates src/styles/tokens.css; `npm run ds:build` copies this file into the Design System.

tokens.name: color-ground
tokens.usage: Page background. Everything sits on it.

tokens.name: color-panel
tokens.usage: Cards, panels and grid cells that hold content.

tokens.name: color-raised
tokens.usage: Selected tab, hover fill, tag fill, skeleton blocks.

tokens.name: color-inset
tokens.usage: Image placeholders and recessed wells. Text on inset is color-ink or color-ink-2; color-ink-3 falls below 4.5:1 here in Paper.

tokens.name: color-hairline
tokens.usage: 1px rules and card borders. Structure, never meaning.

tokens.name: color-hairline-strong
tokens.usage: Quote rules, unfilled meter bars, table header rules.

tokens.name: color-control-edge
tokens.usage: Borders of inputs and secondary buttons. 3:1 on ground and panel in both themes.

tokens.name: color-ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and headlines on ground, panel and raised.

tokens.name: color-ink-2
tokens.usage: Secondary text, descriptions, quotes. 6:1 or better on every surface.

tokens.name: color-ink-3
tokens.usage: Labels, captions, the grey half of the POV headline. 4.6:1 or better on ground, panel, raised and the tints in both themes. In Paper it falls below 4.5:1 on color-inset (4.26:1) and on color-signal-soft over the ground (4.47:1): use color-ink-2 there (Label tone="strong").

tokens.name: color-signal
tokens.usage: Modus violet. The one thing to look at: the bottleneck bar, the active tab line, the selected ring. Marks and large type only.

tokens.name: color-signal-text
tokens.usage: Violet as text: links, a highlighted figure, the bottleneck label.

tokens.name: color-signal-soft
tokens.usage: Fill behind a highlighted cell, answer block or future-state panel. Small text on it is color-ink, color-ink-2 or color-signal-text: color-ink-3 falls to 4.47:1 over the ground in Paper.

tokens.name: color-signal-line
tokens.usage: Border of a highlighted cell.

tokens.name: color-on-signal
tokens.usage: Text set inside a color-signal fill.

tokens.name: color-action
tokens.usage: Primary button fill: Modus violet 500 in both themes. One primary action per view.

tokens.name: color-action-hover
tokens.usage: Primary button on hover: one step darker, the same in both themes.

tokens.name: color-on-action
tokens.usage: Text and icons on color-action.

tokens.name: color-focus
tokens.usage: Focus ring: 2px solid, 3px offset, on every interactive element.

tokens.name: color-mark
tokens.usage: Neutral data marks: the bars that are not the story.

tokens.name: color-mark-soft
tokens.usage: Decorative marks inside product-as-illustration panels only.

tokens.name: color-dot
tokens.usage: The 16px dot grid behind hero panels (.mi-dots).

tokens.name: color-positive
tokens.usage: Good news, always with an icon or word.

tokens.name: color-negative
tokens.usage: Pain points and bad deltas, always with an icon or word.

tokens.name: color-tint-violet
tokens.usage: A grouping tint: it marks one kind of content, always with its word or icon, and means one thing per project. OpportunityCard uses it for Build-new; elsewhere it often holds a question to react to.

tokens.name: color-tint-mist
tokens.usage: A grouping tint, as color-tint-violet. OpportunityCard uses it for Evolve-ways-of-working.

tokens.name: color-tint-sage
tokens.usage: A grouping tint, as color-tint-violet: a third kind of content, such as a first test or a next step. Used sparingly.

tokens.name: color-logo
tokens.usage: The Modus Create logo's ink, exactly as supplied: black on Paper, white on Ink. Only for the logo — never for text or UI.

tokens.name: color-violet-900
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp. Brand moments: CTA bands, the cover.

tokens.name: color-violet-800
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp. Text on violet-100.

tokens.name: color-violet-700
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp.

tokens.name: color-violet-500
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp. The pop.

tokens.name: color-violet-300
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp. Violet on dark grounds.

tokens.name: color-violet-100
tokens.usage: Modus violet ramp. Light brand tile.

styles.name: display-xl
styles.usage: One per page: the name of the thing.

styles.name: display-l
styles.sample: Claims start fast and finish slow.
styles.usage: The POV headline, once per page. Continue the sentence in color-ink-3 for a two-tone line: the only two-tone line on the page.

styles.name: display-m
styles.sample: Simple claims wait behind complex ones.
styles.usage: Chapter and section titles: the section's claim, in one tone.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Card titles, panel headings and a chapter's closing question.

styles.name: statement
styles.sample: Adjusters re-key the same loss details into three systems.
styles.usage: An insight statement. One sentence, a claim.

styles.name: body-l
styles.sample: Twelve interviews and five ride-alongs point to the same pattern.
styles.usage: Reading text and hero subheads. Keep to a 620px measure.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Waiting for documents, reserves and an approval nobody owns.

styles.name: ui-l
styles.sample: Days from first notice to first payment
styles.usage: Exhibit and group titles (with font-semibold) and an emphasised line in a card. Takes its line height from its context; add leading-snug where it wraps.

styles.name: ui-m
styles.usage: Figure titles, row names, the product name in the top bar and large button labels.

styles.name: ui-s
styles.usage: Links, legends, metadata, table cells, tabs and small button labels.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Uppercase annotations that add what the heading doesn't: an ID and a status, a qualifier (Illustrative data), a FIG number the text cites, a table head. Always uppercase. Not an eyebrow over every heading.

styles.name: tag
styles.usage: The words inside a Tag: always uppercase. A touch tighter than label, because the tag's edge already sets it apart.

styles.name: figure-xl
styles.usage: The one hero number on a view.

styles.name: figure-l
styles.usage: A stat tile: one per view, unless it reads a model's results.

spacing.note: A 4px scale that matches Tailwind's spacing unit: p-4 is space-4 (16px).

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Gap between meter bars and icon-to-text.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Gap between tags and small controls.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Gap between buttons; table cell padding.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Gap inside cards between rows.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Grid gap between cards.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Card padding.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Gap between a section title and its content.

tokens.name: space-10
tokens.usage: Hero panel padding.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Gap between related sections.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Page side gutter on desktop.

tokens.name: space-24
tokens.usage: Gap between chapters.

tokens.name: radius-tag
tokens.usage: Tags, keyboard hints, meter bars.

tokens.name: radius-control
tokens.usage: Inputs, list rows, small tiles.

tokens.name: radius-panel
tokens.usage: Cards and panels.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Buttons, segmented tabs and switches.

shadow.note: Elevation comes from surface steps and hairlines. The one shadow is for overlays.

tokens.name: shadow-overlay
tokens.usage: Dialogs, the Ask palette and popovers only.

layout.note: Pages are one composed column, designed at 1440px. On big monitors the whole column grows, headline included, so its proportions hold; it never runs edge to edge.

tokens.name: layout-column
tokens.usage: Width of the page column, its padding included: 1440px on laptops; from 1680px-wide windows it grows with 120px margins each side, up to 1920px. Beyond that the margins grow and the column stays centred.

tokens.name: layout-gutter
tokens.usage: Padding inside the page column: 16px on phones, 64px from 1280px wide.

tokens.name: layout-measure
tokens.usage: Maximum width of reading text and form fields, whatever the window.

tokens.name: layout-rail
tokens.usage: Width of the sticky chapter rail beside long pages.

tokens.name: layout-hero
tokens.usage: Size of the one POV headline per page: 40px on phones, 64px on laptops, then growing with the page column up to 85px so it keeps its three-line stack.
